ModelCharacter: The unconventional coastal Krogen: a very wide, full-beam 36-footer built around interior volume rather than offshore passagemaking. The Manatee feels closer to a compact floating cottage than a traditional narrow trawler, with a huge salon, one large stateroom and extremely economical single-diesel operation.
DesignLineage: Kadey-Krogen introduced the Krogen 36 Manatee in 1984 as a coastal cruiser rather than a bluewater passagemaker.
Its broad, full-beam salon and lack of exterior side decks distinguish it sharply from the company's classic raised-pilothouse offshore trawlers.
The single-stateroom arrangement became far more popular than the original two-stateroom layout.
The Manatee is a distinct design branch and not a shortened version of the Krogen 42.
OwnershipCharacter: Mechanically simple and exceptionally economical, with excellent liveaboard room for its length. The tradeoffs are limited side-deck circulation, very slow speed and 1980s systems/structure that make survey condition more important than drivetrain complexity.

ModelVariations.Name: 2005–14 generation
ModelVariations.Description: All-new, wider Meridian 341 Sedan introduced for 2005.

ModelCharacter: Meridian's entry-level bridge cruiser, but really two distinct boats under one model number. The 2003–04 version is essentially the Bayliner 3488 Command Bridge rebadged as Meridian; the 2005–14 generation is a completely new, wider two-stateroom yacht with far more interior volume and almost no conventional side decks.
DesignLineage: The first Meridian 341 (2003–04) directly continues the Bayliner 3488 Command Bridge hull, accommodations and flybridge layout.
An all-new 341 Sedan arrived for 2005 with greater beam, new styling, revised two-stateroom interior and different hull geometry.
The 2003–04 and 2005–14 boats therefore share a marketed model number, not a common hull.
Both generations fit Meridian's core formula of affordable flybridge living space, twin inboards and easy molded-stair bridge access.
OwnershipCharacter: The later 341 is extremely roomy for its nominal size but achieves that volume by minimizing side decks and carrying considerable machinery/system density. Twin gas inboards are common; diesel examples exist. Thrusters, bridge systems, generator, HVAC and tight access make it more complex than a simple sedan of similar length.

ModelVariations.Name: Sea Raider / Tri-Cabin transition
ModelVariations.Description: Introduced as the 36 Sea Raider; became the all-fiberglass 36 Tri-Cabin from 1972.

ModelCharacter: One of Trojan's longest-running family motor yachts: a 36-foot modified-V aft-cabin cruiser with three separated living zones, twin inboards, wide walkaround decks and a large social flybridge. Most were gasoline-powered and cruised in the mid-teens, making it a classic Great Lakes/coastal motor yacht rather than a trawler.
DesignLineage: The model began in 1970 as the 36 Sea Raider, initially using a solid-fiberglass hull with wood deckhouse.
For 1972 Trojan moved to all-fiberglass construction and the model became the 36 Tri-Cabin.
Several interior generations followed; a major 1986 update added walkaround double berths in both staterooms and a U-shaped galley.
Production continued through 1987, making the F-36 Tri-Cabin one of Trojan's longest-lived fiberglass models.
OwnershipCharacter: Huge living space for 36 feet and a very active owner community make these boats easy to understand and improve. Twin gasoline engines dominate the fleet and can be expensive to feed; diesel examples are uncommon. Fuel tanks, exhausts, decks, wiring and V-drive/direct-drive differences need hull-specific verification.
